voiceover: Here's one of the most fascinating arguments for God's existence — and it comes from mathematics. Look closely at the universe and you find something strange: it obeys mathematics, with eerie, decimal-point precision. Why should it? Take one example. In 1854 a mathematician dreamed up a bizarre, useless-looking curved geometry — pure abstraction, no use in sight. Sixty years later it turned out to be the exact language of Einstein's gravity. And this keeps happening. The math even runs ahead of us: in 1962 it predicted a particle nobody had ever seen — and two years later, they found it. A Nobel physicist, Eugene Wigner, called this 'the unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics,' and admitted there is no rational explanation for it. His own words for it? 'A wonderful gift which we neither understand nor deserve.' He reached for one word: miracle. So here's the argument. A universe written in elegant mathematics makes far more sense if a rational Mind wrote it than if it's a blind accident. A gift implies a giver. And the most natural reading of a cosmos written in reason is that Reason wrote it.
